tip_clearance.quote: Not stated anywhere in the report (text, figures, Tables I-VI, appendixes). No cold or running clearance given.

value.IGV: zero camber (Table V(a): KIC, KTC, KOC, TOTAL CAMBER all .00)

profile_types.quote: Blades having low inlet relative Mach numbers (all stators and rotor 3), were of double circular arc (DCA) shape. Blades having supersonic inlet relative Mach numbers (the midspan to tip regions of rotors 1 and 2) were of multiple circular arc (MCA) shape.

profile_definition.value: two-segment centerline with constant change of angle with path distance per segment; MCA when C1 != C2; DCA when C1 = C2 and max thickness at midchord
profile_definition.quote: Each blade element is composed of two segments. The blade centerline (mean camber line) and the two surfaces of each segment have a constant change of angle with path distance (fig. 10). A blade element is completely specified by the following: leading- and trailing-edge angles, Kle and Kte, and radii, Rle and Rte; maximum thickness Tm; location of maximum thickness Cm and transition point CT; and the turning rate ratio C1/C2. When C1 ≠ C2, the blade element shape is described as multiple circular arc (MCA). When C1 = C2 and the maximum thickness is at midchord, the blade shape is a double circular arc (DCA).

mca_turning_ratio.quote: The MCA blade shapes are specified by rotor blade-element inlet to outlet mean camber line turning ratios of less than 1.0.

max_thickness_location.quote: All rotor and stator blades for compressor 74A are thickest at midchord and have small leading-edge wedge angles.

blade_element_surfaces.value: conical surfaces through the streamline locations
blade_element_surfaces.quote: The blade elements are defined on conical surfaces which pass through the blade streamline locations (fig. 9).

stacking.value: centers of area along a prescribed stacking line; fabrication planes perpendicular to a radial line through the hub stacking point
stacking.quote: After the blade elements are defined, they are stacked about their centers of area along a prescribed stacking line. For manufacturing purposes fabrication coordinates are given on planes perpendicular to a radial line through the hub stacking point.

igv.value: zero camber (all blade angles .00), zero design incidence and deviation, variable
igv.quote: For the IGV's design incidence angles are set at 0 relative to the blade mean camber line. ... For the IGV design deviation angles are 0.

variable_rows.quote: The compressor's IGV and stator blade setting angles were variable and reoriented to achieve maximum overall adiabatic efficiency, using a vane reset optimization computer code.

igv_design_loss.quote: For the IGV's, a radially constant 2 percent drop in total pressure is used.

design_incidence.quote: For the three rotors of the inlet stage group, the design suction-surface incidence angles are all 0. For the stators the design suction-surface incidence angles were from -1.0° to -3.0°.

designed_vs_built.quote: For the first three stages of this five-stage core compressor, an additional aeromechanical design was completed. This inlet three-stage group was fabricated and evaluated experimentally.

design_pressure_ratio_5stage.quote: Core compressor 74A has five stages and is designed for a 9.271:1 pressure ratio and 29.710-kg/sec flow.

design_pressure_ratio_3stage.quote: The inlet stage group had a design pressure ratio of 4.474 and design efficiency of 0.799.

design_efficiency_3stage.quote: The inlet stage group had a design pressure ratio of 4.474 and design efficiency of 0.799.

design_mass_flow.quote: An aerodynamic design is presented for a five-stage core compressor with a 9.271 pressure ratio and 29.710 kg/sec flow rate.

design_specific_flow.quote: At the rotor 1 inlet tip speed was 430.291 m/sec, annular flow was 193.173 kg/sec m2, and hub to tip radius ratio was 0.488.

rotor1_inlet_hub_tip_ratio.quote: At the rotor 1 inlet tip speed was 430.291 m/sec, annular flow was 193.173 kg/sec m2, and hub to tip radius ratio was 0.488.

blockage.value: 0.04 at rotor 1 inlet rising to 0.14 at stator 5 outlet, applied equally to hub and tip
blockage.quote: The blockage factor for compressor 74A, expressed as a fraction of local annular area, was equally applied to the flow-path hub and tip. Total blockage (see fig. 4) increases from 0.04 at the rotor 1 inlet to 0.14 at the stator 5 outlet.

inlet_preswirl.quote: No preswirl was used for compressor 74A.

value.inlet: plenum: two iron-constantan thermocouples; four manifolded wall static taps ~90 deg apart; inlet total pressure assumed equal to plenum static
value.outlet: four rakes ~90 deg apart, 6.8 cm downstream of the third-stage stator row; five total-pressure/total-temperature elements at 10, 30, 50, 70, 90 percent span from the outer casing; static pressure from linear variation between inner and outer wall statics

measurement_stations.quote: The compressor outlet conditions were determined from measurements obtained from four rakes located ~90° apart 6.8 cm downstream of the third-stage stator row. Each rake had five total-pressure-total-temperature elements located at 10, 30, 50, 70, and 90 percent span from the outer casing.

test_inlet_pressure.quote: both inlet butterfly throttle valves were partially closed to maintain a constant compressor inlet pressure of 5.066 N/cm2

test_speeds.quote: Data were recorded at 60, 70, 80, 85, 90, 95, and 100 percent of design speed.

reset_schedules.value: tabulated in figure insets: Fig. 18 design settings (all 0); Fig. 21 IGV +15, S1-S3 +10 at all speeds; Fig. 22 per speed (see CSVs)
reset_schedules.quote: The design speed peak adiabatic efficiency was obtained by resetting the IGV's +15° and each stator blade row +10° (fig. 20).

reset_sign_convention.value: shown only graphically in Figure 20 (top view, positive reset rotation arrow); no verbal definition
reset_sign_convention.quote: Figure 20.—Schematic of blade rows with positive direction of vane reset specified.

measured_overflow.quote: Because the large overflow (9.1 percent of design flow) at design speed was inconsistent with past experience in predicting choke margin for transonic rotors

materials.quote: The rotor blades were made of titanium (TI-GAL-4V), and the stator blades of maraging steel (18 NI 200).

value.CONE ANGLE: angle between axial direction and conical surface representing blade element, deg
value.TOTAL CAMBER: difference between inlet and outlet blade-element angles on mean camber lines, deg (KIC-KOC)
value.DELTA INC: difference between mean camber blade angle and suction-surface blade angle at leading edge, deg
value.PHISS: suction-surface camber ahead of assumed shock location, deg
value.TURNING RATIO: ratio of mean camber line curvatures upstream and downstream of transition point
value.CHOKE MARGIN: ratio of flow area greater than critical area to critical area
